scenes.text: You probably think of the Sahara Desert as an endless wasteland of dry sand.
Every twenty-one thousand years, a wobble in Earth's axis completely flips the African monsoon season.
Suddenly, torrential rains pour over the dunes, transforming this massive desert into a lush green paradise filled with lakes and flowing rivers.
In fact, deep beneath the hot sand lies a massive network of fossilized rivers, just waiting for the water to return.
